text: Damage Control Bridgade - feudal authority tasked with peacefully maintaining public order, combating crime and ensuring the safety of its citizens.
A fiefdom the Middle Moor. It's your homeland: it raised you, punished you, and comforted you -- like a good parent.

A Feudocratic form of government established after the Rifle Strike. It classifies territories as Productive Fiefdoms (PF) or Stale Fiefdoms (SF) based on their productive capacity and self-sufficiency. Each Fiefdom is expected to own its means of production and provide for itself independently.

This doctrine sees individual freedom and cooperation as the means to achieve social equality, thereby creating a society without a leader, a state, or God. Some refer to it also as "the sweetest form of altruism".

The natural satellite of Sintesi. In children's fairy tales, it is often described as a giant onion floating in space; however, recent analyses from fallen fragments have shown the presence of chymosin and casein, and therefore of cheese.

It consists of sixty days or twelve quints, and six Arcs form a Cycle. Since the Rifle Strike, Arcs have been named after members of the New Youth. The last one, however, is named after Ermak Panin, the founder of Feudocratism.
Beautiful but Deplorable - ancient artifacts from the pre-feudocratic eras. Produced by the private sector, memorabilia of the deplorable capitalism.
Productive Fiefdom across the sea. It now lies in ruins: the CoFoPo attack brought the entire fief to its knees using a Miasmic bomb — the same fate befell Moravika shortly after.

One of the ten districts of Lundonstoch. The inhabitants of Brickingham are well-known for their counter-culture — based on "tagging" and choppy haircuts — along with their strong sense of belonging to the land and disdain for authority. It is one of the four districts to border Eggmuth.
A spherical and tiny planet, Lundonstoch and the Middle Moor are on it. And you too.
A gigantic sphere, eternally in flames. It warms Sintesi and marks the rhythm of its inhabitants. The Djesoti believe it to be the dwelling place of their God.
A radio programme hosted by Copper Jack and Silver Kurt, broadcast live from the Seabrim Tower.
A time frame for Sintesi to revolve around Tesi. The division into day, quint, and arc is an ancient tradition dating back to the Tongue Epoch.
A time unit equal to five days. Twelve quints fit into an Arc. Seventy-two quints in a Cycle. To put it plainly, cancer will take you away in two hundred and seventeen quints.

A democratically elected District Military Representative. They are the quintessential embodiment of the saying "Judge, Jury, and Executioner". The Burgrave takes part in the Knowtorath's assemblies to decide inter-fiefdom policies.

The legal authority of a Dormitory. The appointed individual is responsible for maintaining order and fostering cooperation among residents, in accordance with the laws set forth in the Condominium Constitution.
Feudal institution for Health Care; it handles free treatment and care for the fief's sick. That's where they gave you the joyful news: you have cancer.
The Cauldron House is one of the Damage Control Brigade’s (DCB) local stations scattered across the fiefdom’s districts.

Feudal maintenance institution; it handles repairs to public infrastructure, mostly Dormitories. The wait times between request and intervention are so long that they have a dedicated wisecrack category.
House of the Department of Feudocratic Inspiration; useful should you ever entertain the morbid notion that CoFoPo ideology isn't that bad.
Acronym for "Multi-Magnetic Screwdriver." It is the standard-issue tool given to the Condo-Chief of each dormitory.

Subversive union backed by hundreds of Stale Fiefdoms; they're said to have agents in every Productive Fief, and their ranks keep swelling in every State. Their aim is to impose a diet rich in Miasmic bombs, along with all the nutrients necessary to subvert the status quo.
A Djesota phrase commonly used in the fiefdoms of Fablarica and D'Oil. Literally translated, it means "Accepting one's fate with love".

1602nd–1754th Cycle. A troubled era, marked by the Holyvolution -- born from the D’Oilan Rebellion in the name of the God Djesok -- and the Progressive Breeze, an intellectual movement that rewrote the social rules of the Altomare Empire.
Name of the fiefdom of Lundonstoch before the Rifle Strike; its capital was Loondvohn, now identifiable as the Newborne District.

A political ideology; the orgiastic child of the patriotism, ambition and cult of strength throuple. The emblem of the individual who never needs to ask, for he acts upon his own present and that of others.

An interfeudal security organisation formed by the world’s largest Productive Fiefdoms. Now dissolved, its purpose was to contain the territorial expansion of fiefdoms and prevent the formation of sovereign states and nations.
Political-economic doctrine based on the personal freedom of every citizen, the privatization of the market, and individual choice.

A period spanning the 1754th to 1821st Cycle, marked by the “gift” of faeces in silver sent to D’Oilands by Loondvohn and Eckimborough. The gesture sparked the Nine-Cycle War and the dreaded Yellow Pest.

One of the ten districts of Lundonstoch, where the dev class lives. Those are the spiritual descendants of the martyr and founding father Layton, the Inventor. Its prestigious techno-philosophical academies effectively make it the industrial and sanitary engine of the Fiefdom.
The Land of God, Wine and Revolutions; twin sister and eternal arch-rival of Lundonstoch. It lies on the east coast of the Middle Moor, overlooking the Revanche Sea.
Charitable association for food distribution to the poor, which translates into stale bread, stewed onion, and double-malt beer - great diet.
They perform anything the Condo Chief obeys and desires. Their duties include coordinating maintenance work, listening to residents' complaints, and distributing meals.
The Dev Class is composed of individuals concentrated on the growth of the industrial-sanitary industry. Devs can be "loaned" between Fiefdoms to establish a trust based on technological cooperation.
Third Arc of a Cycle. It takes its name from Devereux, known as "the Professor" and founding father of Lundonstoch. It is better known as the Jujube harvest season.
The means by which man can sail the skies and impose borders there as well. It is a rigid-structure airship, whose flight is made possible by the gas that flows through it.
Djesok is the last god to have outlasted time, revered by the fiefdoms of D'Oil, Fablarica and Vernacolo; it is depicted as a figure shrouded in a mantle, with a mirrored visage.
One of Lundonstoch’s ten districts, pressed against the dangerous border with D’Oil. Its streets teem with immigrants and simmering tensions: a powder keg waiting for a spark.
One of the three Productive Fiefdoms of the Middle Moor besides Lundonstoch and D'Oil. During the Cunning Ages it was known as Eckimborough.

One of Lundonstoch’s ten districts, bordering Eggmuth. Castles from the Tongue Epoch rise above ancient forests, fields and farmsteads, forming vistas worthy of the Melancholic painters. These lands supply 70% of the fiefdom’s timber.

The Fiefdom’s historical research institute, dedicated to the study, preservation and interpretation of its past. Its scholars oversee archives, recover ancient records and artefacts, and piece together what remains of the world before the Shatter.
Sixth Arc of a Cycle. It takes its name from Ermak Panin, author of the Feudocratist Manifesto. Ermonath marks the pruning season of the Purple Primrose.
A makeshift radio lockpick that cracks Radio-Locks by fishing for their frequency. Illegal, unreliable and easy to conceal, it changes hands across the fiefdom’s black markets.
Foreign Productive Fiefdom across the sea. Its citizens are known for being passionate, straightforward, and, well, quick with a knife.
Temporary anti-abortion law; it was passed by referendum on the last day of Lundonstoch's Onion Festival. It was an extreme measure to counter the low birth rate — it remains in force to this day.
Theorised by the philosopher Ermak Panin, this political and economic ideology saw decentralisation and de-privatisation as the only solution to the bondage of capitalist society.
Fifth Arc of a Cycle. It takes its name from Fitzory, Lundonstoch's Founding Father. Fitzmonath is the harvesting season for Bald Strawberries.
Acronym for "Feudal Pneumatic Transfer System", it is a device that enables communication between a building and external feudal services.
Famous pub, a gathering spot for the workers of Factory No. 3. Located in the Wynnstan District.

Term used to indicate the Feudocratic Government, i.e. the executive and decision-making apparatus of the Feudal Republic of Lundonstoch. It is composed of 10 Margraves (one per district), and operates based on the Principle of Unanimity.
A travelling company of musicians journeying across seas, mountains and fiefdoms, in search of Musical Artefacts left behind by the Intangible Musicians, those who come from another world.

Devereux was the only Founding Father not to die by gunshot, impalement or fire. He saw Feudocratism as a flawed yet salvageable system, to be corrected through moderation and state oversight of private enterprise rather than its demonisation. Holisticism emerged as the cure to this ailment.

The epoch of the First Global War (1821st–1828th Cycle). The Oceanic Wall starved the planet Sintesi and seven Cycles of war killed 240 million people. It ended with the Rifle Strike and the rise of Feudocratism.
First Arc of a Cycle. It takes its name from Juno, Lundonstoch's Founding Mother. Jumonath is the harvesting season for Plum Bells.

Term used to indicate anyone guilty of inter-feudal espionage against a Fiefdom's Technological Knowledge. Their aim is to steal Research and Development Dossiers, but they may go as far as kidnapping or murdering a prominent Dev.
Also known as "Lundonstoch's Feudal Intelligence", it is the fief's military management apparatus.

Fourth Arc of a Cycle. It takes its name from Layton, one of Lundonstoch's Founding Fathers. It is the harvesting season for Poppybeans, which are very popular among Devs for their nootropic properties.
Foreign Productive Fiefdom across the sea. It now lies in ruins: the CoFoPo attack brought the entire fiefdom to its knees using a miasmic bomb — the same fate befell Berlhen shortly before.
Stands for "Maintenance Personal Pipe System". Boiler with independent controls: the tenant can adjust it however they like. Prone to breakdowns, it requires regular maintenance.
It refers to the New T-Based music that emerged in Cunningstan in the 1999º cycle. The themes range from playfulness and hedonism, to the use of joy as an act of resistance.

One of the ten districts of Lundonstoch and the only one built using red brick for each of its buildings. Here resides the political class of the Fiefdom, which is a curious coincidence given the massive presence of lupanars, that is, houses of pleasure.

This refers to the era of T-Based great classics from the 1828º to the 1999º cycle. The themes were simple and melancholic, yet deeply rooted in maritime life and its hardships. The most popular ensemble was Lundock's BustedCylinder.
Foreign Productive Fiefdom across the sea.
An identification document issued by the fiefdom in which the individual intends to settle. Depending on the applicant's situation, a colour and corresponding rights are assigned.
Lundonstoch's main energy source. Peat is extracted from the surrounding marshy areas near the border with the Gap.

A criminal enterprise based in Lundonstoch, it controls the Black Market. It is allegedly run by the Percivals, a shady family with the peculiar tradition of giving the same name to brothers, sisters and cousins.
One of the few private companies in Lundonstoch; it was founded by Ilionor di Gavin during the Empty Age -- after a hundred cycles it still produces the Gavin's Glue and the Gavin's Lube.
A symbol formed by joined hands to resemble a plucked, wounded, fallen raven. It is used to convey, without words, that a comrade should be left alone to recover on their own.
Second Arc of a Cycle. It takes its name from Polyanna, Lundonstoch's Founding Mother. Polymonath is the mating season for crows. Too bad you won't see Good Luke getting laid.
Acronym for "Personal Pneumatic Transfer System", it is a device that enables communication within the same building, but not with the outside world.
An electro-hydraulic device used to convert pressure variations into electrical signals. It opens Pressure-locks.
An electro-hydraulic device used to secure doors or storage containers; it can be opened using a mapped Pressure Booster.
RFID-based lock. It is a passive radio-frequency receiver.
Referendum on expanding the DBC presence and arms production against the CoFoPo threat. YES won with 73%.

A low-cost technology that uses radio waves to unlock doors or safes; it operates over very short distances. There is usually a passive receiver on standby, known as the "lock", and an active transmitter, known as the "key".

The worldwide Feudocratic Revolution of the 1828th cycle. Weary of cycles of gruelling war, soldiers from all over laid down their rifles and stormed the government buildings of their respective nations, coordinated by their New Youth movement. This led to the end of the First Global War and the concept of State and Nation.

Your time: fragmented and formless, with only isolated organs in secret rebellion against one another. Its starting point is marked by the Rifle Strike in the 1828th cycle. It is so named, due to the ‘fragmentation’ it had on the global economy and politics. There have been no wars for two hundred cycles.
The primordial epoch, before time and speech. Before the original flesh broke apart and became man.
A land of dreary hills and hundreds of small Stale Fiefdoms, between D'Oil, Lundonstoch and Eggmuth. It stretches across half of the Middle Moor. Its inhabitants are known as Gappers.
Everlasting oblivion upon death; the cold grasp of void. What matters in Lundonstoch is what you have done for the Fief, what you have passed on to future generations. There is no God here.

A direct consequence of the First Global War's latter stages. It takes its name from the Miasma bomb and strikes fear into the hearts of anyone who hears its mention. Fortunately, it never actually happened, due to the large-scale mobilisation of the Rifle Strike.
It indicates the island between the southern and northern hemispheres of Thesis; it includes the fiefdoms of Lundonstoch, D'Oil and Eggmuth. Divided only by the Gap, they live in a fragile harmony.

Composed of burning hearts and intrepid spirits, it was the underground organisation that put a stop to the Miasmic Threat with the Rifle Strike. The Lundonstoch faction was led by Juno, Polyanna, Fitzroy, Layton and Devereux.

Lasting until the 1411th Cycle, it saw mankind gather into ever larger communities, from tribes to the first cities. Charles of Gheudogal’s pilgrimages among different peoples inspired the idea of Feudal Society and, later, the Fiefdom of D’Oil.
Foreign Productive Fiefdom across the sea.

The Oceanic Wall was a pressure strategy to weaken USATZIA's economy set up by the Eastern Conjunction - it was ineffective: USATZIA struck a deal with Wajian leaving the Middle Moor on the verge of famine.
A citizen serving in the armed force of Lundonstoch aka DCB; they are the personification of the arms and the truncheon of the Grand Feudal Council.
Foreign Productive Fiefdom across the sea.

The Epoch between the 1411º and 1602º cycles, in which man knew the hunger for expansion but never sated it; and in which the first Fief in history also arose: D'Oil, under Charles of Gheudogal, later becoming an Empire. During this Epoch, the first grand war fought for an idea and not for someone took place: the Biennale War between the Altomare Empire and the D'Olian Empire.
One of the ten districts of Lundonstoch, Walden seems frozen in the Age of Tongue: Eggmuthian castles, watchtowers and old fortresses overlook the great lakes and the Brown Forest.

One of the ten districts of Lundonstoch. If you ever find yourself lost in the Fiefdom, Wulfstan is the worst place: its labyrinthine alleyways criss-cross the area, effectively turning it into a puzzle impossible to solve. Fortunately, it's also packed with pubs and friendly comrades who're more than willing to show you the way out in exchange for a pint of beer.

One of Lundonstoch’s ten districts. Factory smog chokes its streets beneath a greenish haze, with the Sea Bream Tower and the colossal statue of Juno rising as its main landmarks. You have lived here for 43 Cycles.

An epidemic that struck the Middle Moor in the 1750º cycle. Most believe it was caused by the silly habit of Lundoneers' comrades to celebrate a war victory by shitting on corpses. Faeces, cadavers and seagulls apparently are not a good soup.

A period of interfeudal tensions beginning in the 1997th Cycle, marked by crises such as the closure of the KnowTradeMarket. Nearly thirty Cycles later, from its fractures emerged the idea of a new order: Confeudocratism.

People's Deputy. Each district elects one. This representative legislates on the internal policies of their own district, but not on those concerning neighbouring districts, and represents the district in the Grand Feudal Council.
A civil servant working for Grand Feudal Council's bodies. The symptoms of office work include glassy eyes, bored expressions, and a complete lack of will to live.
A derogatory term used to refer to an individual with a 'Yellow Passfief'. They have no right to vote.
An individual in possession of a 'Green Passfief'. They exercise full rights and are a fully-fledged citizen of Lundonstoch.

One of Lundonstoch’s ten districts, White Vessel is the maritime heart of the DCB. Its ports dispatch the ships that patrol the ocean and the Fiefdom’s borders. Orderly, guarded and well-kept, it is among the city’s more respectable districts.

One of the ten districts of Lundonstoch, but certainly the worst for seagull droppings. The population, consisting of fishermen, has now joined the CoFoPo cause, effectively turning it into a rebel district.
An individual in possession of a 'Red Passfief'. Without permits or right to say in the fiefdom.
A military and economic alliance comprising the nations of Rushkya, Vergerber, Boldenisle, D'Oilands, Denorstd, Gola and Conceptìon. It collapsed in 1828 during the Rifle Strike.
KnowTradeMarket, where it is possible to lend, sell and buy tech-health knowledge between Productive Fiefdoms. Access is prohibited to Stale Fiefdoms.
A military and economic agreement laid down before the Shattered Epoch. The Western United Forces consisted of the nations of USATZIA and Vindica.

A musical genre born in the Lundock district amongst sailors and workers of the shipyards; to ease the work, they carried portable brass instruments and sang along, with only their ears and instinct to guide them.
